claims.feature: other: sentimentality as a named risk
claims.claim: Oden reports that critics sometimes fault Kay for being too sentimental and too romantic, and partly concedes the charge.
claims.source: Scott Oden (novelist), 'A Quarter Turn', Towers of Spider-Haunted Mystery (Substack), 2026
claims.quote: Critics sometimes hit Kay for being too sentimental, too romantic
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'Critics sometimes hit Kay'

claims.claim: A tabletop-RPG forum reader says Kay's narrator commentary and foreshadowing often felt heavy-handed to him.
claims.source: 'Uqbarian', post #19 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: his narrator commentary and foreshadowing often felt really heavy-handed to me

claims.claim: The same reader says Kay is a top-notch prose stylist who goes on rather more than he needs to.
claims.source: 'Uqbarian', post #19 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: he just goes on rather more than he needs to

claims.claim: The same reader reports a scene in The Lions of Al-Rassan of characters thinking portentous thoughts for five and a half pages.
claims.source: 'Uqbarian', post #19 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: thinking portentous thoughts for five and a half pages

claims.claim: Another forum reader says the renamed real cities of The Last Light of the Sun left him constantly mixing up not-Constantinople and not-Jerusalem.
claims.source: 'Daztur', post #10 in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: constantly get not-Constantinople and not-Jerusalem mixed up

claims.claim: A forum reader says The Lions of Al-Rassan moves between an adventure story and a people-living-through-history story.
claims.source: 'Gavin Bennett', quoted post in 'Talk to me of Guy Gavriel Kay', RPGnet forum, 2022
claims.quote: a sort of adventure story and a people living through history

claims.claim: A reviewer says that while he enjoys Kay's prose he often wishes there was less of it.
claims.source: 'Brok3n Engines', review of Tigana, Brok3n Engines (Substack), 2025
claims.quote: while I enjoy his prose, I often wish there was less

claims.claim: Kay says the subject engaging him is that a novel you read is a story being told to you by someone.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: a story being told to you by someone
claims.page: answer to 'So what interests a more mature ... Kay nowadays?'

claims.claim: Kay says he is fascinated by how we examine and remember the past and shape the narratives we need from it.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: how we examine and remember the past
claims.page: answer to 'So what interests a more mature ... Kay nowadays?'

claims.claim: Kay says he would be more an architect than a gardener because the shape of a novel matters a lot to him.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: the shape of a novel matters a lot to me

claims.claim: Kay says setting came first for A Brightness Long Ago.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, interviewed by Patrick St-Denis, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.quote: I think setting came first here
claims.page: answer about A Brightness Long Ago's arc of emergence

claims.claim: The interviewer reports Kay having said that in general setting precedes theme, which grows out of learning about time and place.
claims.source: Patrick St-Denis (interviewer), paraphrasing Kay's earlier answer, Pat's Fantasy Hotlist, 2019
claims.page: interviewer's question about A Brightness Long Ago

claims.claim: Kay warns readers to be sceptical when writers present intuitive processes as thought-out planning.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'On the Strengths of Fiction Done as Near-History' (first published at boingboing.net, 2016), Bright Weavings
claims.quote: be skeptical when writers present intuitive processes as thought-out planning
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'There are a multiplicity of reasons'

claims.claim: Kay says he always includes starter bibliographies in his novels.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'On the Strengths of Fiction Done as Near-History' (first published at boingboing.net, 2016), Bright Weavings
claims.quote: And I always include starter bibliographies
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'And I found that I liked'

claims.claim: Kay says each reader makes the book they read.
claims.source: Guy Gavriel Kay, 'On the Strengths of Fiction Done as Near-History' (first published at boingboing.net, 2016), Bright Weavings
claims.quote: each reader makes the book they read
claims.page: body, paragraph beginning 'And I found that I liked'

verdicts.trueWording: "Critics sometimes hit Kay for being too sentimental, too romantic, too invested in beauty and tragedy and doomed nobility. And yeah, there's some of that."
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200, browser UA). Byline 'Scott Oden', Towers of Spider-Haunted Mystery, Feb 23 2026 — matches source. Quote appears word for word; the partial concession limb is carried by 'And yeah, there's some of that.' (followed by 'But I think the criticism misses something.').

verdicts.trueWording: "In particular, his narrator commentary and foreshadowing often felt really heavy-handed to me."
verdicts.note: Raw thread page fetched (HTTP 200). Found in post #19 by Uqbarian, Jun 26 2022 — post number and date match. forum.rpg.net is a tabletop-RPG forum, so that limb holds. ('him' is the researcher's pronoun; the poster writes 'to me' and states no gender.)

verdicts.trueWording: "He is a top-notch prose stylist, but he just goes on rather more than he needs to."
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same post #19 (Uqbarian, Jun 26 2022) — 'the same reader' limb confirmed by shared post. Quote verbatim; both limbs (top-notch stylist, goes on too long) are in one sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: "Al-Rassan has a scene of key characters just looking at each other and thinking portentous thoughts for five and a half pages."
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same post #19. Quote verbatim. 'Al-Rassan' is The Lions of Al-Rassan — named in full in the Gavin Bennett post quoted immediately above it in the same post.

verdicts.trueWording: "...so I don't have to constantly get not-Constantinople and not-Jerusalem mixed up."
verdicts.note: Raw page, post #10 by Daztur, Jun 25 2022 — post number and date match. Quote verbatim; the renaming and The Last Light of the Sun limbs are in the same post ('I found The Last Light of the Sun incredibly annoying. If you're going to have Rome, Jerusalem, Constantinople... just call them...'). Poster's gender is not stated on the page.

verdicts.trueWording: "it moves interestingly between a sort of adventure story and a people living through history story"
verdicts.note: Raw page. Written by Gavin Bennett in post #9 (Jun 25 2022) and re-quoted inside Uqbarian's post #19 (Jun 26 2022), as the source's page hint says. Subject is 'The Lions of Al-Rassan', named in the preceding sentence.

verdicts.trueWording: "But the truth is that, while I enjoy his prose, I often wish there was less of it."
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200); full body text present, no paywall. Brok3n Engines review of Tigana, Apr 16 2025 — matches source. Quote verbatim as final-paragraph clause. The reviewer's gender is not stated on the page ('he' is the researcher's pronoun).

verdicts.trueWording: "That whole subject of storytelling, that a novel you read is a story being told to you by someone ..."
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Quote verbatim in Kay's answer to 'So what interests a more mature and hopefully wiser Guy Gavriel Kay nowadays?' — the exact question the source names — and Kay frames it as 'what is engaging me', supporting the 'subject engaging him' limb.

verdicts.trueWording: "I'm fascinated by how we examine and remember the past ... and shape narratives we need or want from that."
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same answer. Quote verbatim. Page says 'narratives we need or want from that'; the claim's 'the narratives we need from it' drops 'or want' but does not overstate.

verdicts.trueWording: "I'd be more an architect because the shape of a novel matters a lot to me (as a reader, too)."
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim in Kay's answer to the George R. R. Martin architects-or-gardeners question, so both the architect-over-gardener limb and the reason limb are supported.
Same raw page. Quote verbatim; 'here' is anchored by the interviewer's immediately preceding line 'How was it for A BRIGHTNESS LONG AGO?', so the book limb holds.

verdicts.trueWording: "You replied that in general setting precedes theme (which grows out of learning about time and place)"
verdicts.note: Same raw page. Quote verbatim, and it does sit in the interviewer's (Patrick St-Denis's) question rather than in Kay's own words — exactly as the claim attributes it.

verdicts.trueWording: "But here's a caveat: be skeptical when writers present intuitive processes as thought-out planning."
verdicts.note: Raw page fetched (HTTP 200). Bright Weavings, posted Dec 10 2016, header line 'This first appeared at http://boingboing.net/ in 2016' — provenance limb confirmed. Quote verbatim in the paragraph beginning 'There are a multiplicity of reasons', as the source's page hint says.

Same raw page, in the paragraph beginning 'And I found that I liked' — page hint matches. Quote verbatim. 'In his novels' is not literal on the page but the whole essay is about his own novels and the sentence sits among his readers' post-reading history reading.

verdicts.trueWording: "well, each reader makes the book they read"
verdicts.note: Same raw page, same paragraph beginning 'And I found that I liked'. Quote verbatim.
